dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: ātmano nirvikārasya kva jñānaṃ kva ca vā kriyā | jñānāyattā bahirbhāvā ataḥ śūnyam idaṃ jagat ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: In the unchanging Self, where is knowing and where is acting? External things depend on knowing; therefore this world is empty.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh (on 133–134 together): the Self is one mass of consciousness without change; knowing and acting, in the sense of the limited individual's changing, difference-ridden knowing and acting, cannot belong to it, and external objects depend on them, so the world is empty; contemplating so, one acquires peace. The knowing and acting that belong to the Self are its powers (jñāna-śakti, kriyā-śakti), not dependent on mind or senses. Wallis counts verse 134 as 'not a yukti'.
dharana.technique_name: The Unchanging Self: This World Is Empty
dharana.instruction: Rest as the unchanging awareness behind all knowing and doing, and see the world as empty.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 109' = verse 134 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 134 = 'The world is ‘empty’ (not a yukti)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 134 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 134: The world is ‘empty’ (not a yukti)
numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 134 'Dharana 111', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 109. Not followed.
numbering_variants.wallis_grouping: Wallis marks verse 134 '(not a yukti)': he does not count it as a technique. Singh comments on 133 and 134 together but gives each its own dhāraṇā heading (108, 109); The Mystery Within's Session Two list does the same.

source_disagreements: Status as a technique: Singh counts verse 134 as dhāraṇā 109 (with a shared commentary on 133–134); Wallis marks it 'not a yukti'.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 134 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the world that depends on them, seen as empty
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a still centre that does not change, with the moving world of knowing and doing seen as empty around it.
geometry.svg_hint: a still point at the centre of faint, moving lines that fade
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Rest in the unchanging
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention rests in what does not change, and the changing world of knowing and doing is seen as empty. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The unchanging awareness in which knowing and acting come and go
attention.secondary: The world, which depends on knowing, seen as empty

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: In the unchanging Self, where is knowing and where is acting? External things depend on knowing; therefore this world is empty.
adiyogi.method_summary: Notice that knowing and doing keep changing, while the awareness in which they appear does not. Rest as that unchanging awareness. See the world, which depends on being known, as empty of solid reality.

honesty.disclosure: Door 109 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 109 (verse 134) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 109 is dharana 109, verse 134. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. A philosophical contemplation; if it feels heavy, let it go and rest with the breath. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
